objects.description: Abstract allocator interface used internally by FlatBuffers' vector_downward container. Implementations must provide allocate and deallocate for raw byte buffers. The default reallocate_downward grows buffers only (new_size > old_size), allocates a new region, copies the front and back in-use regions downward via memcpy_downward, and frees the old region. memcpy_downward is a protected utility that copies the specified front and back slices into the new buffer layout. Intended for downward-growing buffers; not a general-purpose realloc. Ownership, lifetime, and thread-safety semantics are not specified here and depend on the concrete implementation.
Unsigned offset types used in FlatBuffers wire format. uoffset_t is the 32-bit standard offset; uoffset64_t is a 64-bit variant for large buffers.
Signed offsets used for references that may be negative (e.g., vtable references). 32-bit default with a 64-bit variant.
Unsigned 16-bit type used for indices/offsets within vtables in FlatBuffers objects.
Alias for the largest available unsigned integer type on the target (uintmax_t). Useful for generic scalar handling.

Template wrapper around uoffset_t representing a relative Offset to a FlatBuffers object of type T. Allows 0 to represent a null reference. Provides helpers to check nullability and to obtain the untyped union form. Size is asserted to be 4 bytes.
Type trait that evaluates to true_type if the given type is a specialization of flatbuffers::Offset<>, otherwise false_type. Useful for SFINAE and overload resolution within FlatBuffers internals.
Template wrapper around uoffset64_t representing a 64-bit relative offset to a FlatBuffers object of type T. Allows 0 to represent null. Size is asserted to be 8 bytes.
Type trait that evaluates to true_type if the given type is a specialization of flatbuffers::Offset64<>, otherwise false_type. Used for internal template specializations.

Family of helper templates that abstracts reading elements from vectors in FlatBuffers. Primary template handles scalars, specialization for Offset/Offset64 handles vectors of offsets, and SFINAE-based specialization handles vectors of structs stored inline. Provides typedefs for return types and element stride and static Read() functions.

objects.definition: typedef uoffset_t offset_type;
objects.description: Inner typedef inside Offset<T> naming the underlying unsigned offset scalar type (32-bit). Note: This is a nested alias, not a standalone top-level type; include here for completeness as defined in the header. Usage is Offset<T>::offset_type.

objects.definition: typedef uoffset64_t offset_type;
objects.description: Inner typedef inside Offset64<T> naming the underlying unsigned 64-bit offset scalar type. Note: This is a nested alias, not a standalone top-level type; usage is Offset64<T>::offset_type.

objects.definition: struct BufferRefBase {};  // for std::is_base_of
objects.description: Empty base struct used solely as a common base for BufferRef<T> so type traits like std::is_base_of can recognize BufferRef<T> objects. It contains no data and provides no ownership or behavior.

Concrete allocator implementation in the flatbuffers namespace that uses C++ new[]/delete[] for byte buffers. It inherits from Allocator (declared elsewhere) and provides allocate and deallocate; it also provides a static dealloc helper compatible with callbacks taking (void*, size_t). No additional state; instances are lightweight.

RAII owner for a completed FlatBuffer memory region detached from its builder. Holds the raw buffer, its current data start pointer, size, total reserved capacity, and the allocator used to allocate it. It frees the buffer via Deallocate(allocator_, buf_, reserved_) on destruction and optionally deletes the allocator if own_allocator_ is true. Copy is disabled; move construction/assignment transfer ownership and null out the source. Provides data(), size(), and begin()/end() accessors for read/write access to the contiguous byte range.

Options container for code generation. Holds the output path for generated files and an optional FileSaver used to persist outputs. Construction is aggregate; file_saver may be null to indicate default saving behavior as determined by the generator.

Abstract interface for generating source code from FlatBuffers schemas or binary schema (bfbs). Implementations provide language-specific generation by overriding the pure virtual methods. Not copyable; has a virtual destructor. Includes an inner Status enum and a status_detail string for error context.

Enumeration of result codes returned by CodeGenerator methods. Nested within CodeGenerator. Note: as an enum type, it is not instantiable via pointers in typical use; pointer form shown per schema requirements.

Abstract interface for saving data associated with a file name. Provides a pure-virtual SaveFile method that writes a buffer (or std::string overload) and an optional Finish hook. Copy is disabled; move is allowed. Intended to be subclassed to implement concrete saving behavior (e.g., real file I/O or collecting names).
Concrete FileSaver that writes data to real files on disk. Implements SaveFile; no additional state is stored in the header. Finish uses base default (no-op).

Concrete FileSaver that records the names of files passed to SaveFile instead of (or in addition to) actually writing them. Maintains an internal set of file names and provides a Finish override, likely to flush or expose collected names. Exact persistence behavior is not specified in this header.

Primary FlatBuffers builder class template. Provides APIs to construct FlatBuffer-serialized data. The Is64Aware template parameter controls whether 64-bit offsets are supported and enforces ordering constraints when mixing 32/64-bit regions. Manage buffer growth, alignment, vtable creation/deduplication, vectors, strings, structs, finishing, and releasing buffers.

objects.definition: using FlatBufferBuilder64 = FlatBufferBuilderImpl<true>;
objects.description: Alias of FlatBufferBuilderImpl configured for 64-bit offsets (Is64Aware = true). Enables creation of Offset64-returning objects and enforces serialization of 64-bit region before 32-bit items.

struct EmptyOffset {};
objects.description: Tag/placeholder struct used to disambiguate StartVector overloads for the 64-bit builder without constructing real offsets. Contains no fields.
Template comparator for inline structs that provide KeyCompareLessThan; used to sort structs when creating sorted vectors.
Template comparator for table Offsets using each table’s KeyCompareLessThan for ordering; used to create sorted vectors of tables. Holds a reference to the builder’s buffer for temporary access.

objects.definition: struct NativeTable {};
objects.description: Base class marker for native (de-serialized) FlatBuffers object types. It contains no data or behavior; used purely as a tag type.
Packed 16-bit descriptor for a field’s type in minimal reflection data: base elementary type, repetition (vector/array), and optional index into a sequence/type reference table.

Minimal reflection table describing a FlatBuffers type. Includes kind (table/struct/union/enum), element count, per-field TypeCode array, optional referenced type functions, array sizes, value lists, and names.

objects.definition: typedef const TypeTable* (*TypeFunction)();

objects.description: Alias for an 8-bit float placeholder used when reading sized scalars as floating point. Currently represented as 8-bit integer; no 8-bit float semantics implemented.
Base class for FlexBuffers accessors. Holds a pointer to data and the element byte width for the object view.
Accessor for objects that carry a size prefix (e.g., strings, blobs, vectors). Computes size from the prefix or accepts a manual size.
View over a FlexBuffers string (size-prefixed, UTF-8 by convention). Provides c_str, length and convenience helpers.
View over a FlexBuffers blob (size-prefixed arbitrary bytes).
View over an untyped FlexBuffers vector (size-prefixed sequence of elements each followed by a type table). Provides random access via Reference.
View over a typed FlexBuffers vector (all elements share the same Type; no per-element type table).
View over a fixed-length typed vector (length 2–4). Elements are tightly packed with known byte width and no size prefix.
View over a FlexBuffers map (vector of values with prefixed keys vector). Provides keyed lookup using binary search over shared keys.
Dynamically typed handle to any FlexBuffers value. Provides type tests, conversions, mutation for scalars/strings (when size permits), and navigation to complex types.
Flags configuring FlexBuffers::Builder sharing behavior for keys, strings, and key vectors to reduce buffer size.

Serializer for FlexBuffers. Accumulates values on a stack, builds vectors/maps/strings/blobs, supports typed/fixed vectors, sharing of keys/strings, and finishes a buffer ready for reading with GetRoot(). Nested struct Builder::Value represents a pending/serialized value.
Internal value descriptor used by Builder to compute storage widths, write values/offsets, and carry minimal bit-width information for elements and vectors.

Runtime verifier that checks structural integrity of a FlexBuffers buffer, including offsets, sizes, types, nesting depth, alignment (optional), string termination, and shared key/string reuse (optional tracker).

Abstract visitor interface used to iterate (mini-reflect) over FlatBuffers objects without requiring full schema reflection. Methods are invoked during traversal of tables/structs, vectors, and individual scalar/string/union values. Users subclass this to implement custom behavior (e.g., pretty-printing).

Concrete IterationVisitor that builds a human-readable string representation of a FlatBuffer object, approximating JSON. Supports optional multiline output, indentation, quoting of names, and vector formatting. Use with IterateFlatBuffer/IterateObject.
FlatBuffers reflection type descriptor. Encodes a base type, element type (for vectors/arrays), related index into object/enum tables, fixed-length for arrays, and cached size metadata.
Builder helper to construct a reflection::Type table into a FlatBuffer.
Generic key/value attribute pair used to annotate schema items with custom metadata.

objects.description: Enumeration of all FlatBuffers base types used in reflection, including scalars, String, Vector/Array, Object (table/struct), Union, and helper markers.
Bitflag enum indicating which advanced schema language features are used by the compiled schema.

Convenience class in namespace flatbuffers that registers FlatBuffers schemas by file identifier and provides conversions between FlatBuffer binaries and text using those schemas. It owns a registry of schemas (path strings) and parsing/output options. Usage: call Register for each schema identifier/path, optionally SetOptions and AddIncludeDirectory, then use FlatBufferToText or TextToFlatBuffer. Errors are available via GetLastError.
Alias of std::true_type (or its local equivalent).
Alias of std::false_type (or its local equivalent).
A tag type representing an empty Optional state, with a constant instance flatbuffers::nullopt provided.

FlatBuffers string container stored inline within a FlatBuffer. It derives from Vector<char>, providing string-friendly accessors (c_str, str, optional string_view) and a strict-weak-order operator< using StringLessThan. It represents a length-prefixed, non-null-terminated byte sequence; c_str returns a pointer to the underlying data (not necessarily null-terminated). Construction is typically performed by FlatBuffers builders; manual construction is not intended.

Opaque, non-owning view over a FlatBuffers inline struct payload. Provides typed accessors into the underlying byte array for fixed-layout structs that lack vtables. Construction is restricted (private constructors); instances are typically obtained by pointing at existing buffer memory. GetField<T> reads a scalar at byte offset o. GetStruct<T> returns a reinterpret_cast<T> pointer at byte offset o for nested structs. GetAddressOf provides raw byte pointer access. Alignment and bounds safety are the caller’s responsibility.

A lightweight view class over a FlatBuffers table. Provides methods to read, write, and verify fields and offsets using a vtable stored preceding the table data. Instances are obtained by pointing at existing buffer memory; construction, copying, and assignment are private to prevent owning semantics. The underlying memory is not owned by Table and must remain valid for the lifetime of its use. Alignment/verification helpers integrate with VerifierTemplate to validate serialized data.

Singleton helper that owns a C locale object used to perform locale-independent strto* conversions when FLATBUFFERS_LOCALE_INDEPENDENT is enabled. It stores a platform-specific locale handle and exposes it via Get(). Constructors/destructor are declared here but defined elsewhere.
Enumeration of naming/casing styles used by FlatBuffers utility functions (e.g., ConvertCase) to transform identifiers between styles.

kPathSeparator is a constexpr char constant defined as '/'. It is not a user-defined type; no standalone definition block applies. Alias included here only to acknowledge its presence; treat as built-in char. Details unknown beyond value.

objects.definition: struct String;
objects.description: Forward declaration of flatbuffers::String. Only declared here, not defined. Likely represents a FlatBuffers UTF-8 string object elsewhere.
Type-erased FlatBuffers vector view used with reflection to access vectors of unknown element type. Not constructible directly; points into a buffer and exposes size() and raw Data().

A templated FlatBuffers buffer verifier. When TrackVerifierBufferSize is true, it additionally tracks the highest accessed offset to compute the minimal valid buffer size. Provides methods to verify alignment, vectors, strings, tables, offsets, and nested FlatBuffers. Includes nested Options configuration struct. Two concrete aliases are provided: SizeVerifier (tracking enabled) and Verifier (tracking disabled unless build macro maps it to SizeVerifier).

objects.definition: using SizeVerifier = VerifierTemplate</*TrackVerifierBufferSize = */ true>;
objects.description: Type alias for VerifierTemplate with size tracking enabled. Supports GetComputedSize to report the minimal valid buffer size after verification.

Primary verifier alias. By default aliases VerifierTemplate with size tracking disabled for speed; when FLATBUFFERS_TRACK_VERIFIER_BUFFER_SIZE is defined (deprecated), it aliases SizeVerifier instead.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Allocator::reallocate_downward
functions.signature: virtual uint8_t* reallocate_downward(uint8_t* old_p, size_t old_size, size_t new_size, size_t in_use_back, size_t in_use_front);
functions.description: Reallocates a buffer for flatbuffers’ downward-growing vector_downward. Allocates a new block of new_size bytes, copies the in-use regions from the front (in_use_front) and back (in_use_back) of the old buffer, deallocates the old buffer, and returns the new pointer. Unlike a standard realloc, this grows downward and copies two disjoint regions of the old buffer.
requirements: new_size must be greater than old_size; this is enforced via FLATBUFFERS_ASSERT(new_size > old_size).
old_p must point to a block of exactly old_size bytes previously allocated by this same allocator (inferred from use of deallocate(old_p, old_size)).
in_use_front bytes from the start of old_p and in_use_back bytes from the end of old_p must be valid to read and intended to be preserved (explicitly described).
The preserved regions must not overlap: in_use_front + in_use_back must be less than or equal to old_size (inferred from copying logic).
Caller must not use old_p after this call returns, as it will be deallocated by this function (stated by code behavior).
Function relies on allocate(new_size) and deallocate(old_p, old_size) to succeed according to the allocator’s semantics; behavior on allocation failure is allocator-specific/unknown.

functions.name: flatbuffers::GetSizePrefixedRoot
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename SizeT = flatbuffers::uoffset_t> const T* flatbuffers::GetSizePrefixedRoot(const void* buf)
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the root object of type T within a size-prefixed FlatBuffer. It skips the size prefix of type SizeT and then locates the root object, similar to GetRoot.
requirements: buf must be non-null; the function performs pointer arithmetic before any null checks.
buf must point to the start of a size-prefixed FlatBuffer where the first sizeof(SizeT) bytes encode the total size prefix.
After the size prefix, the remaining bytes must form a valid FlatBuffer whose root object type is T.
Environment endianness must match FlatBuffers expectations (checked in debug builds).
Returned pointer must not be used to modify the underlying data.

functions.name: flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::BufferRef
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty BufferRef that references no buffer (buf == nullptr, len == 0) and does not own any memory (must_free == false). Typically used to create a handle that will be filled later before calling GetRoot() or Verify().
requirements: After default construction, buf is nullptr and len is 0; calling GetRoot() on a nullptr buffer is invalid and must be avoided.
Before using GetRoot() or Verify(), the caller must assign buf and len to point to a valid FlatBuffer containing a root of type T.
If the caller sets must_free to true later, buf must point to memory allocated with a free()-compatible allocator.

functions.name: flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::BufferRef
functions.description: Constructs a BufferRef that references an existing buffer at _buf of length _len bytes. The BufferRef does not take ownership by default (must_free == false). Use GetRoot() to access the root object of type T or Verify() to validate the buffer.
requirements: _buf may be nullptr only if _len is 0; otherwise _buf must be a valid pointer to at least _len bytes of readable memory.
The memory must contain a FlatBuffer whose root type is T if the caller intends to use GetRoot() or Verify().
Ownership: The constructed BufferRef does not own the buffer (must_free == false). If the caller later sets must_free == true, the memory must be allocated with a free()-compatible allocator.

functions.name: flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::~BufferRef
functions.description: Destructor. Frees buf with free() only if must_free is true; otherwise it is a no-op. BufferRef does not own memory by default.
requirements: If must_free is true at destruction time, buf must either be nullptr or point to memory allocated with a free()-compatible allocator.
The caller must not cause double-free by externally freeing buf when must_free is true or by sharing the same allocation across multiple BufferRef instances that may set must_free.
Threading/lifetime: Ensure no other code uses buf after the BufferRef is destroyed if it owned the memory.

functions.name: flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::GetRoot
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const T* flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::GetRoot() const
functions.description: Returns a typed pointer to the root object T stored in the referenced FlatBuffer using flatbuffers::GetRoot<T>(buf). No validation is performed.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to a FlatBuffer whose root type is T.
The buffer must remain valid and readable for as long as the returned pointer is used; the pointer becomes invalid if the underlying buffer is freed or mutated.
Call Verify() (or perform equivalent validation) before dereferencing the returned object to avoid undefined behavior on malformed data.

functions.name: flatbuffers::BufferRef<T>::Verify
functions.description: Verifies that the referenced buffer is a valid FlatBuffer containing a root of type T using flatbuffers::Verifier and VerifyBuffer<T>(nullptr). Returns true if verification succeeds, false otherwise.
requirements: buf must point to the start of the FlatBuffer and len must be the total size of the buffer in bytes.
_No ownership change_: Verify() does not modify buf, len, or must_free.
If buf is nullptr or len is insufficient, verification will fail and the function returns false; callers should not use GetRoot() on a buffer that fails verification.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::allocate
functions.description: Allocates a contiguous array of size bytes using operator new[]. Intended as the default FlatBuffers allocator for buffer/storage creation when no custom Allocator is supplied.
requirements: size must be >= 0; behavior is undefined for excessively large sizes that exceed available memory

Returned pointer must be freed with the matching deallocation routine (flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::deallocate or flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::dealloc) or via flatbuffers::Deallocate with a null allocator
The allocation is an array of uint8_t created with new[]; callers must not free with free() or delete (without [])

functions.name: flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::deallocate
functions.description: Deallocates memory previously allocated by DefaultAllocator::allocate using delete[]. The size parameter is ignored by this implementation.
requirements: p must be a pointer previously returned by flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::allocate (or otherwise allocated as uint8_t[] via new[])
p may be null (delete[] on null is a no-op)
Do not pass memory allocated by a different allocator or freed elsewhere
The size argument is unused by this implementation, but some Allocator implementations may require the correct size

functions.name: flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator::dealloc
functions.description: Static convenience deallocator that deletes a buffer allocated as a uint8_t array via new[]. Useful as a C-style callback/deleter where a void* and size are provided.
requirements: p must point to memory allocated as a uint8_t[] array using new[] (e.g., via DefaultAllocator::allocate)
p may be null
size is ignored by this implementation

functions.name: flatbuffers::Allocate
functions.description: Allocates size bytes using the provided allocator if non-null; otherwise uses the DefaultAllocator. This allows callers to pass a null Allocator* to mean "use the default" without owning an allocator instance.
requirements: If allocator is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to an object implementing flatbuffers::Allocator with a working allocate(size_t) method

If allocator is null, allocation is performed via flatbuffers::DefaultAllocator and must be deallocated accordingly (using flatbuffers::Deallocate with allocator == null, or DefaultAllocator::deallocate)
size must be >= 0; very large sizes may fail with bad_alloc

functions.name: flatbuffers::Deallocate
functions.signature: void flatbuffers::Deallocate(flatbuffers::Allocator* allocator, uint8_t* p, size_t size)
functions.description: Deallocates memory previously obtained via flatbuffers::Allocate with the same allocator pointer. If allocator is null, frees using the DefaultAllocator. The size is forwarded to the allocator (ignored by DefaultAllocator).
requirements: allocator must be the same pointer that was used for the corresponding allocation; if allocation was done with allocator == null, pass null here as well
p must be a pointer previously returned by the matching allocator’s allocate (or null)
If a custom allocator requires size for deallocation, pass the correct size; DefaultAllocator ignores size
Do not mix allocators: memory allocated by one allocator must not be deallocated with another

functions.name: flatbuffers::ReallocateDownward
functions.signature: uint8_t* flatbuffers::ReallocateDownward(flatbuffers::Allocator* allocator, uint8_t* old_p, size_t old_size, size_t new_size, size_t in_use_back, size_t in_use_front)
functions.description: Reallocates a buffer to new_size using the provided allocator (or DefaultAllocator if allocator is null), moving existing contents in a manner consistent with Allocator::reallocate_downward semantics used by FlatBuffers’ downward-growing buffers. Typically preserves two regions of in-use data near the back and front of the buffer while shifting to the end of the new allocation.
requirements: allocator must be a valid flatbuffers::Allocator implementing reallocate_downward, or null to use DefaultAllocator’s implementation
old_p must be either null or a pointer to a buffer allocated by the same allocator with size old_size
new_size should be sufficient to hold in_use_back + in_use_front bytes; behavior is allocator-defined if insufficient
in_use_back and in_use_front must not exceed old_size and should describe the actual live data regions to be preserved
Do not pass memory allocated by a different allocator
The returned pointer may differ from old_p; callers must use the returned value and abandon old_p after success

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::DetachedBuffer
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty DetachedBuffer that does not own any memory. All internal pointers are null and sizes are zero. Typically used as a placeholder to be assigned/moved into later.
requirements: No arguments or special preconditions.
After construction, data() may return nullptr and size() is 0; callers must handle an empty buffer.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::DetachedBuffer
functions.signature: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::DetachedBuffer(flatbuffers::Allocator* allocator, bool own_allocator, uint8_t* buf, size_t reserved, uint8_t* cur, size_t sz)
functions.description: Constructs a DetachedBuffer that takes ownership of a finished FlatBuffer memory region. The buffer and allocator pointers are stored so the DetachedBuffer can manage the memory lifetime (deallocate on destruction and optionally delete the allocator). Intended to wrap a pre-built buffer without a builder.
requirements: allocator must be the allocator that was used to allocate buf (inferred from usage of Deallocate(allocator, buf, reserved)).
If own_allocator is true, allocator must be heap-allocated and suitable for deletion via operator delete; it will be deleted in the DetachedBuffer destructor.
buf must point to the start of the allocated memory block of size at least reserved bytes (inferred).
reserved must reflect the total number of bytes allocated at buf (inferred).
cur must be the start of the valid data region within the allocation; sz is the number of valid bytes starting at cur (inferred).
If sz > 0, cur is expected to be non-null and within the memory block described by buf/reserved (inferred).
Callers must not free or reuse buf or allocator while the DetachedBuffer is alive; the DetachedBuffer assumes responsibility for freeing buf and possibly deleting allocator.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::DetachedBuffer
functions.description: Move-constructs a DetachedBuffer, transferring ownership of the underlying allocation and allocator from other. The source is reset to an empty state.
requirements: other is left in a valid but empty state after construction; do not use its previous pointers after the move.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from another DetachedBuffer, first destroying any currently owned resources, then taking ownership of other's allocation and allocator. The source is reset to an empty state.
requirements: Self-move-assignment is safe; the operator guards against it.
After assignment, other is left empty; do not rely on its previous contents.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::~DetachedBuffer
functions.description: Destroys the DetachedBuffer, deallocating the owned buffer via Deallocate(allocator, buf, reserved) if present, and deleting the allocator if own_allocator is true. Leaves the object reset to an empty state.
requirements: The allocator provided at construction must be valid for use with Deallocate for the given buf and reserved (inferred).
If own_allocator was true, allocator must be deletable via delete.
After destruction, pointers obtained from data()/begin()/end() become invalid.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::data
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the start of the valid data region of the detached buffer. May be nullptr if the buffer is empty.
requirements: Caller must handle a possible nullptr when the buffer is empty.
The returned pointer remains valid until the DetachedBuffer is destroyed or moved from.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::data
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the start of the valid data region of the detached buffer. May be nullptr if the buffer is empty.
requirements: Caller must handle a possible nullptr when the buffer is empty.
Mutating the returned memory must remain within size() bytes.
The returned pointer remains valid until the DetachedBuffer is destroyed or moved from.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes in the valid data region of the detached buffer.
requirements: None beyond having a valid DetachedBuffer instance.
If size() is 0, data()/begin()/end() may be equal and data() may be nullptr.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::begin
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the first byte of the buffer’s valid data region (same as data()). Provided for iterator-style access.
requirements: May return nullptr if size() == 0; callers must handle that.
Do not dereference unless size() > 0.
Mutations must stay within [begin(), end()).

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::begin
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the first byte of the buffer’s valid data region (same as data()). Provided for iterator-style access.
requirements: May return nullptr if size() == 0; callers must handle that.
Do not dereference unless size() > 0.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::end
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer one past the last byte of the buffer’s valid data region (data() + size()). Provided for iterator-style range semantics.
requirements: If data() is nullptr, end() equals nullptr + size(), which is only safe to use for comparisons; do not dereference end().
Use only for iterator-style bounds; never dereference the returned pointer.

functions.name: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer::end
functions.description: Returns a const pointer one past the last byte of the buffer’s valid data region (data() + size()). Provided for iterator-style range semantics.
requirements: If data() is nullptr, end() equals nullptr + size(), which is only safe to use for comparisons; do not dereference end().
Use only for iterator-style bounds; never dereference the returned pointer.

functions.description: Virtual destructor for CodeGenerator. Allows safe deletion through a base-class pointer and proper cleanup by derived generators. The destructor is defaulted in the interface and typically performs no work unless overridden by a derived class.

If derived classes allocate resources, they must release them in their own destructors (typical C++ inheritance requirement).

functions.name: flatbuffers::CodeGenerator::GenerateCode
functions.signature: virtual flatbuffers::CodeGenerator::Status GenerateCode(const flatbuffers::Parser& parser, const std::string& path, const std::string& filename) = 0

requirements: parser must reference a successfully parsed FlatBuffers schema and remain valid for the duration of the call.
path should be a writable filesystem path where generated files can be created.

functions.name: flatbuffers::CodeGenerator::GenerateCodeString

requirements: parser must reference a successfully parsed FlatBuffers schema and remain valid for the duration of the call.
output is an out-parameter that may be modified; callers should not rely on its prior contents being preserved.
Because the base implementation returns Status::NOT_IMPLEMENTED, callers should handle that status and/or call this only if the generator advertises support (e.g., via documentation).

path and filename should correspond to the location/name of the schema or outputs as expected by the generator.

functions.name: flatbuffers::FileSaver::SaveFile
functions.signature: virtual bool SaveFile(const char* name, const char* buf, size_t len, bool binary) = 0;
functions.description: Abstract interface method to save a buffer to a file. Implementations (e.g., RealFileSaver or FileNameSaver) define how data is handled. Callers pass a file path, a pointer to a buffer, its length in bytes, and whether the data should be treated as binary. Returns true on success and false on failure. Usage: invoke on a FileSaver instance to persist data or record the file name, depending on the concrete implementation. Details of error conditions are implementation-defined and not specified here.
requirements: name must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string representing the target file path (inferred from signature and common patterns).
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (inferred from signature).
len is the number of bytes to write from buf (inferred from signature).
binary selects binary vs text mode handling; its exact effects are implementation-defined (inferred).
Caller should check the boolean return value and handle failures appropriately (inferred).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; do not assume concurrent calls are safe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: flatbuffers::FileSaver::Finish
functions.description: Optional hook invoked after all save operations; default implementation does nothing. Intended for implementations to finalize work (e.g., flushing, summarizing). Callers may invoke this to allow the saver to finish any pending tasks. Behavior is a no-op for FileSaver unless overridden.
requirements: No parameters and no return value; default implementation has no requirements.
If using a derived saver that overrides Finish, consult that implementation for ordering or state requirements (unknown).

functions.name: flatbuffers::RealFileSaver::SaveFile
functions.signature: bool SaveFile(const char* name, const char* buf, size_t len, bool binary) final;
functions.description: Concrete implementation that writes the provided buffer to an actual file on the filesystem. Returns true on success and false on failure. binary determines whether the file is opened/written in binary or text mode.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C-string path to a file that can be created or opened for writing (inferred from class purpose and signature).
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (inferred).
len is the number of bytes to write (inferred).
binary selects binary vs text mode; platform-specific end-of-line translations or mode flags may apply (inferred).
Caller should check the boolean return value and handle I/O errors (inferred).
Sufficient filesystem permissions and valid path are required; errors are implementation/OS-dependent (inferred).

functions.name: flatbuffers::FileNameSaver::SaveFile
functions.signature: bool SaveFile(const char* name, const char* buf, size_t len, bool binary) final;
functions.description: Concrete implementation that records file names instead of writing data. The buffer contents, length, and binary flag are accepted but presumably ignored; only the file name is saved internally (based on class name and presence of a file_names_ set). Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C-string; it will be recorded in the internal set (inferred from class name and member).
buf, len, and binary are not used for writing in this implementation; callers may pass any values, but they must still be valid per the base interface (unknown specifics; inferred).
Caller should check the boolean return value (inferred).
No filesystem access is required for this saver (inferred).

functions.name: flatbuffers::FileNameSaver::Finish
functions.description: Finalization hook for FileNameSaver. Likely processes or exposes the collected file names (e.g., writing an index or performing a summary), but exact behavior is not specified in the header. Use after all SaveFile calls if you need the saver to finalize any collection-related tasks.
requirements: No parameters and no return value. Ordering or side effects are implementation-specific and not described here (unknown).

functions.name: flatbuffers::GetBufferStartFromRootPointer
functions.description: Computes and returns the start address of a FlatBuffer given a pointer to its root table object. Useful when you have a root pointer and want to manage or free the entire buffer. The function assumes the root has a vtable; do not pass pointers to structs or non-table data.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsInt16

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsInt8
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to int8_t via AsInt64.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsUInt64
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to uint64_t. Supports numeric types, parses strings as unsigned, vectors/maps yield size, null yields 0.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsUInt32
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to uint32_t via AsUInt64.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsUInt16
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to uint16_t via AsUInt64.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsUInt8
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to uint8_t via AsUInt64.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsDouble
functions.description: Converts the referenced value to double. Numeric types are converted, strings parsed to number, vectors/maps yield size, null yields 0.0.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsFloat

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsKey
functions.description: Returns a C string for key or string types by dereferencing the offset; otherwise returns an empty string.
requirements: Only valid when GetType() is FBT_KEY or FBT_STRING; otherwise returns "".
Returned pointer must remain within the lifetime of the underlying buffer.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsString
functions.description: Returns a String view if the reference is a string or key (for key, length is computed to first null); otherwise returns an empty String view.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::ToString
functions.description: Converts the value to a JSON-like string, quoting strings/keys as needed and formatting nested types.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsBlob
functions.description: Returns a Blob view if the reference is a blob or string (strings as bytes); otherwise returns an empty Blob.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsVector
functions.description: Returns a Vector view if the reference is a vector or map; otherwise returns an empty Vector.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsTypedVector
functions.description: Returns a TypedVector view if the reference is a typed vector; otherwise returns an empty TypedVector. Deprecated string-typed vectors are surfaced as key-typed vectors.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsFixedTypedVector
functions.description: Returns a FixedTypedVector view if the reference is a fixed typed vector; otherwise returns an empty FixedTypedVector.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::AsMap
functions.description: Returns a Map view if the reference is a map; otherwise returns an empty Map.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::As
functions.description: Templated converter returning the referenced value as type T. Specializations exist for primitives and FlexBuffers wrapper types.
requirements: T must be one of the supported specializations (bool, integer types, float/double, std::string, flexbuffers::String/Blob/Vector/TypedVector/FixedTypedVector/Map) or behave like those.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::MutateInt
functions.description: Attempts to mutate the referenced scalar to integer value i in-place. Succeeds only if the reference is an int/uint (direct or indirect) and the stored byte width can accommodate the new value.
requirements: Reference must be of type FBT_INT/FBT_INDIRECT_INT/FBT_UINT/FBT_INDIRECT_UINT.
The existing storage width must be sufficient for the new value; otherwise returns false.
The underlying buffer memory must be writable.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::MutateBool
functions.description: Attempts to mutate a boolean value in-place. Succeeds only if the reference is FBT_BOOL and storage width is 1 byte.
requirements: Reference must be of type FBT_BOOL.
Underlying buffer memory must be writable.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::MutateUInt
functions.description: Attempts to mutate the referenced scalar to unsigned value u in-place for uint/int (direct or indirect) refs, if storage width is sufficient.
requirements: Reference must be of type FBT_UINT/FBT_INDIRECT_UINT/FBT_INT/FBT_INDIRECT_INT.
Existing storage width must accommodate the new value; otherwise returns false.
Underlying buffer must be writable.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::MutateFloat
functions.description: Attempts to mutate a float in-place. Succeeds for FBT_FLOAT or FBT_INDIRECT_FLOAT if storage width equals 4 bytes.
requirements: Reference must be FBT_FLOAT or FBT_INDIRECT_FLOAT.
Underlying buffer must be writable.
Mutation fails if stored width is not 4 bytes.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Reference::MutateString
functions.description: Attempts to overwrite the referenced string with str of the same length. Returns false on non-strings or size mismatch.
requirements: Reference must be a non-empty String (not the empty-string sentinel).
len must exactly match the existing string length.
Underlying buffer must be writable.

functions.name: flexbuffers::PackedType
functions.signature: inline uint8_t flexbuffers::PackedType(BitWidth bit_width, Type type)
functions.description: Packs a BitWidth and Type into a single byte (low 2 bits: width, high 6 bits: type).

type must be a valid Type.

functions.name: flexbuffers::NullPackedType
functions.description: Returns the packed representation for a null value with 8-bit width.

functions.name: flexbuffers::GetRoot
functions.signature: inline flexbuffers::Reference flexbuffers::GetRoot(const uint8_t* buffer, size_t size)
functions.description: Parses a FlexBuffers buffer and returns a Reference to the root value by reading the trailer (type and width).
requirements: buffer must point to a complete, valid FlexBuffers buffer of length size (or use Verifier to check).
size must be at least 3 bytes.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::GetBuffer
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the finalized buffer. Asserts if Finish() has not been called.
requirements: Finish() must have been called before accessing the buffer.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::GetSize
functions.description: Returns the current size of the internal buffer (not including any unfinished values).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Clear
functions.description: Resets the builder to an initial state, clearing buffer and state, and resetting internal pools.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Null
functions.description: Appends a null value to the current construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Int
functions.description: Appends a signed integer value to the construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::UInt
functions.description: Appends an unsigned integer value to the construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Float
functions.description: Appends a 32-bit floating-point value to the construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Double
functions.description: Appends a floating-point value (choosing minimal width 32/64) to the construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Bool
functions.description: Appends a boolean value to the construction stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::IndirectInt
functions.description: Writes an int64_t value indirectly in the buffer and pushes a reference to it (FBT_INDIRECT_INT).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::IndirectUInt
functions.description: Writes a uint64_t value indirectly and pushes a reference (FBT_INDIRECT_UINT).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::IndirectFloat
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit float indirectly and pushes a reference (FBT_INDIRECT_FLOAT).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::IndirectDouble
functions.description: Writes a double (or float if width permits) indirectly and pushes a reference (FBT_INDIRECT_FLOAT).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Key
functions.signature: size_t flexbuffers::Builder::Key(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Serializes a key string (null-terminated in buffer), optionally shares it, and pushes a key value onto the stack.
requirements: str must point to len bytes of key characters; a null terminator is written.
If BUILDER_FLAG_SHARE_KEYS is set, identical keys may be pooled and reused.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::String
functions.signature: size_t flexbuffers::Builder::String(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Serializes a string as a blob with size prefix and pushes it on the stack as FBT_STRING. May pool identical strings if sharing enabled.
requirements: str must point to at least len bytes; a null terminator is written after the data.
If BUILDER_FLAG_SHARE_STRINGS is set, identical strings may be pooled.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Blob
functions.signature: size_t flexbuffers::Builder::Blob(const void* data, size_t len)
functions.description: Serializes an arbitrary byte blob (with size prefix) and pushes it on the stack as FBT_BLOB.
requirements: data must point to at least len readable bytes.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::StartVector
functions.description: Marks the start position on the stack for building a vector and returns it.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::StartMap
functions.description: Marks the start position on the stack for building a map and returns it.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::EndVector
functions.signature: size_t flexbuffers::Builder::EndVector(size_t start, bool typed, bool fixed)
functions.description: Completes a vector that started at stack index start. If typed is true, checks all element types match; if fixed is true, emits a fixed-length typed vector.
requirements: start must be a valid index returned by StartVector.
If typed is true, all elements must share the same Type or an assertion may fail.
For fixed true, only lengths 2–4 are supported internally (asserts otherwise).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::EndMap
functions.description: Completes a map started at stack index start. Sorts key-value pairs by key, detects duplicate keys, and emits key and value vectors.
requirements: start must be a valid index returned by StartMap.
Every even-positioned element from start must be a key (FBT_KEY) or an assertion fails.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::HasDuplicateKeys
functions.description: Returns true if the last map closed by EndMap contained duplicate keys (which prevents reliable lookup).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Vector
functions.description: Builds a vector by executing callback f to emit elements between StartVector and EndVector. Returns buffer offset of the vector data.
requirements: f must call builder Add/Value methods to push elements before returning.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::TypedVector
functions.description: Builds a typed vector using callback f (all elements must have identical Type).
requirements: f must emit elements of the same Type; otherwise an assertion may fail.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::FixedTypedVector
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
size_t flexbuffers::Builder::FixedTypedVector(const T* elems, size_t len)
functions.description: Builds a fixed-length typed vector from an array of scalars. Supported lengths are 2, 3, and 4.
requirements: len must be 2, 3, or 4 (asserts otherwise).
T must be a scalar type.
elems must point to at least len elements.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Map
functions.description: Builds a map by executing f to emit alternating Key(...) and value calls, then closes the map.
requirements: f must emit an even number of entries as alternating keys and values; keys must be produced with Key(...).

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::MapElementCount
functions.description: Returns the number of key-value pairs (values count) collected since start, asserting even count.
requirements: start must be a valid index returned by StartMap.
The stack between start and current must contain alternating keys and values; otherwise an assertion fails.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::LastValue
functions.description: Returns the last serialized Value on the builder's stack for potential explicit reuse.
requirements: Must be called when at least one value has been pushed onto the stack.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::ReuseValue
functions.description: Pushes a previously captured Value back onto the stack to reuse its serialized representation.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Undo
functions.description: Removes the last element serialized (call once per value or key to undo).
requirements: There must be at least one element on the stack to undo.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Add
functions.description: Convenience overload that appends a signed integer value.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::operator+=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
void flexbuffers::Builder::operator+=(const T& t)
functions.description: Synonym for Add(t); appends a value to the builder.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::ForceMinimumBitWidth
functions.description: Forces a minimum BitWidth for elements of subsequent vectors/maps to allow in-place mutation later. Call with no args to reset.

functions.name: flexbuffers::Builder::Finish
functions.description: Finalizes the buffer by writing the root value, its type, and root width at the end. Asserts that exactly one root value is present.
requirements: Must be called when exactly one root value has been built (stack_.size() == 1).
Finish should be called once per buffer before GetBuffer().

functions.name: flexbuffers::Verifier::VerifyBuffer
functions.description: Verifies the integrity of a FlexBuffers buffer provided to the Verifier at construction time (root exists, types and offsets are valid, nesting limits honored).
requirements: Verifier must be constructed with a buffer pointer and length. Optional reuse tracker should be sized by the constructor.

functions.name: flexbuffers::VerifyBuffer
functions.signature: inline bool flexbuffers::VerifyBuffer(const uint8_t* buf, size_t buf_len, std::vector<uint8_t>* reuse_tracker = nullptr)
functions.description: Convenience utility that constructs a Verifier for the given buffer and runs VerifyBuffer().
requirements: buf must point to buf_len bytes.
If reuse_tracker is provided, it may be resized to buf_len by Verifier.

functions.name: flexbuffers::VerifyNestedFlexBuffer
functions.signature:
template <bool B>
inline bool flexbuffers::VerifyNestedFlexBuffer(
    const flatbuffers::Vector<uint8_t>* const nested,
    flatbuffers::VerifierTemplate<B>& verifier)
functions.description: Verifies that a FlexBuffers blob stored inside a FlatBuffers byte vector is valid. If nested is null, the function treats the field as absent and returns true. Otherwise it invokes flexbuffers::VerifyBuffer on the contents of the vector, routing the result through verifier.Check(...) and using the verifier's FlexBuffers reuse tracker. Intended for validating optional or nested FlexBuffers fields embedded in FlatBuffers data structures prior to use.
requirements: nested may be null. If null, the function returns true without further checks.
If nested is non-null, it must point to a valid flatbuffers::Vector<uint8_t> whose memory is accessible for nested->size() bytes.
If nested is non-null, the vector's data is expected to contain a FlexBuffers buffer; otherwise verification will fail (function returns false).
verifier must be a valid instance of flatbuffers::VerifierTemplate<B> and remain alive for the duration of the call.
Callers should check the boolean return value and treat false as verification failure (do not consume the nested buffer when false).

functions.name: flatbuffers::HashFnv1
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T flatbuffers::HashFnv1(const char* input);
functions.description: Computes the FNV-1 hash of a null-terminated C-string and returns it as type T. Use to generate deterministic 16/32/64-bit hashes (depending on T) for identifiers or strings. For integral T types supported by FnvTraits (uint32_t, uint64_t), this performs the standard FNV-1 algorithm; other Ts require matching FnvTraits specializations.
requirements: input must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string; embedded NUL bytes terminate hashing
T must have FnvTraits<T>::kFnvPrime and FnvTraits<T>::kOffsetBasis defined (provided for uint32_t and uint64_t in this header)
Function is pure and thread-safe; no side effects

functions.name: flatbuffers::HashFnv1a
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T flatbuffers::HashFnv1a(const char* input);
functions.description: Computes the FNV-1a hash of a null-terminated C-string and returns it as type T. Use to generate deterministic 16/32/64-bit hashes (depending on T) for identifiers or strings. For integral T types supported by FnvTraits (uint32_t, uint64_t), this performs the standard FNV-1a algorithm; other Ts require matching FnvTraits specializations.
requirements: input must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string; embedded NUL bytes terminate hashing
T must have FnvTraits<T>::kFnvPrime and FnvTraits<T>::kOffsetBasis defined (provided for uint32_t and uint64_t in this header)
Function is pure and thread-safe; no side effects

functions.name: flatbuffers::FindHashFunction16
functions.description: Looks up a 16-bit string hash function by name and returns a function pointer matching NamedHashFunction<uint16_t>::HashFunction. Supported names are "fnv1_16" and "fnv1a_16". Returns nullptr if no match is found. Use to dynamically select a 16-bit hash algorithm by name.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string
Name comparison is case-sensitive and must exactly match one of: "fnv1_16", "fnv1a_16"
Caller must handle the nullptr return (no match) before invoking the function pointer
Returned function pointer has signature uint16_t (*)(const char*) and expects a non-null, null-terminated C-string

functions.name: flatbuffers::FindHashFunction32
functions.description: Looks up a 32-bit string hash function by name and returns a function pointer matching NamedHashFunction<uint32_t>::HashFunction. Supported names are "fnv1_32" and "fnv1a_32". Returns nullptr if no match is found. Use to dynamically select a 32-bit hash algorithm by name.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string
Name comparison is case-sensitive and must exactly match one of: "fnv1_32", "fnv1a_32"
Caller must handle the nullptr return (no match) before invoking the function pointer
Returned function pointer has signature uint32_t (*)(const char*) and expects a non-null, null-terminated C-string

functions.name: flatbuffers::FindHashFunction64
functions.description: Looks up a 64-bit string hash function by name and returns a function pointer matching NamedHashFunction<uint64_t>::HashFunction. Supported names are "fnv1_64" and "fnv1a_64". Returns nullptr if no match is found. Use to dynamically select a 64-bit hash algorithm by name.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string
Name comparison is case-sensitive and must exactly match one of: "fnv1_64", "fnv1a_64"
Caller must handle the nullptr return (no match) before invoking the function pointer
Returned function pointer has signature uint64_t (*)(const char*) and expects a non-null, null-terminated C-string

functions.name: flatbuffers::InlineSize
functions.signature: inline size_t InlineSize(ElementaryType type, const TypeTable* type_table)
functions.description: Returns the inline byte-size of a field/element described by the mini-reflection ElementaryType. For primitive scalar types, returns the fixed scalar size. For ET_STRING and table/union sequences it returns 4 (uoffset_t), and for ET_SEQUENCE with ST_STRUCT it returns the struct’s inline size taken from the TypeTable. Used to advance pointers while iterating vectors/arrays.
requirements: type must be a valid ElementaryType value.
If type == ET_SEQUENCE: type_table must be non-null and describe the referenced sequence.
If type == ET_SEQUENCE and type_table->st == ST_STRUCT: type_table->values[type_table->num_elems] must contain the struct inline size (as generated by FlatBuffers).
If type == ET_SEQUENCE and type_table->st is not one of ST_TABLE, ST_UNION, or ST_STRUCT, behavior triggers an internal assertion (do not call in that state).
Callers must not pass mismatched type/type_table pairs (e.g., ET_SEQUENCE with an unrelated TypeTable).

functions.name: flatbuffers::LookupEnum
functions.signature: inline int64_t LookupEnum(int64_t enum_val, const int64_t* values, size_t num_values)
functions.description: Maps a concrete enum value to its ordinal index as defined in a mini-reflection table’s values array. If values is null or the value is not found, returns -1. Used by EnumName to translate raw enum values to name indices.
requirements: values may be null; in that case the function returns enum_val unchanged as -1 sentinel (-1 is returned per implementation).
values, if non-null, must point to an array of length num_values containing the underlying integer values of the enum in declaration order.
enum_val should be representable in int64_t (as per signature).

functions.name: flatbuffers::EnumName
functions.signature: template <typename T> const char* EnumName(T tval, const TypeTable* type_table)
functions.description: Returns the string name for an enum value tval using the provided mini-reflection TypeTable. If the table or its names array is missing, or the value is not present in the table’s values array, returns nullptr.
requirements: type_table must describe an enum type (or be the enum TypeTable attached to the field) with parallel names and values arrays.
type_table may be null; in that case the function returns nullptr.
If type_table->names is null, the function returns nullptr (names not available unless generated with --reflect-names).
tval is converted to its underlying integer and looked up against type_table->values; if not found, nullptr is returned.

functions.name: flatbuffers::IterateObject
functions.signature: void IterateObject(const uint8_t* obj, const TypeTable* type_table, IterationVisitor* visitor)
functions.description: Walks a FlatBuffers table or struct instance described by type_table and invokes callbacks on visitor for each field and value. Supports scalars, strings, structs, tables, unions, and vectors/arrays (including union vectors) using the mini-reflection metadata. Intended for generic pretty-printing or lightweight reflection without loading schemas.
requirements: obj must point to the start of a valid object instance: for ST_TABLE, the object must be a Table root; for ST_STRUCT, obj must point to the struct’s inline data.
type_table must be non-null and correspond to the concrete object at obj (its st must be ST_TABLE or ST_STRUCT for top-level calls).
visitor must be non-null and remain valid for the duration of the traversal.
For ST_TABLE fields, obj must reference a valid FlatBuffer with correct vtable/offsets for the given type_table->num_elems mapping (as generated).
For ST_STRUCT fields, type_table->values[i] must be valid byte offsets to each field within the struct.

Union fields require a preceding utype field; when visiting a union value, the corresponding previous field’s value (prev_val) must be the union type field as laid out by generated code; otherwise an assertion may fire when resolving the union.
When iterating vectors, element memory must be contiguous and large enough for size*InlineSize(elem_type, ref).
The function relies on standard FlatBuffers alignment/offset invariants; callers must only pass buffers built by FlatBuffers or previously validated.

functions.name: flatbuffers::IterateValue
functions.signature: inline void IterateValue(ElementaryType type, const uint8_t* val, const TypeTable* type_table, const uint8_t* prev_val, soffset_t vector_index, IterationVisitor* visitor)
functions.description: Dispatches a single value read according to its ElementaryType and invokes the corresponding IterationVisitor method. Handles scalars, strings, structs, tables, and unions (including union vector elements). For sequences, recursively iterates referenced objects.
requirements: visitor must be non-null.
val must point to the inline storage for the value (for strings/tables/unions this is an offset whose target is read).
For type == ET_SEQUENCE: type_table must be non-null and describe the referenced type; for ST_TABLE and ST_UNION the function reads a uoffset_t from val and dereferences it.
For type == ET_SEQUENCE and ST_STRUCT: val must point directly to the struct inline data of size InlineSize(ET_SEQUENCE, type_table).
For type == ET_STRING: val must contain a valid uoffset_t to a String object within the same FlatBuffer.

For unions (ST_UNION): prev_val must point to the corresponding union type field (uint8_t or a vector<uint8_t> for union vectors); otherwise behavior triggers an internal assertion. If vector_index >= 0, prev_val must point to the union type vector whose index matches vector_index.
vector_index must be -1 for non-vector elements; non-negative only when processing vector elements.

functions.signature: inline void IterateFlatBuffer(const uint8_t* buffer, const TypeTable* type_table, IterationVisitor* callback)
functions.description: Traverses the root object of a FlatBuffer and invokes callback through the mini-reflection iteration machinery. This is a convenience wrapper around IterateObject(GetRoot<uint8_t>(buffer), ...).
requirements: buffer must point to a complete, valid FlatBuffer whose root type matches type_table.
type_table must be non-null and correspond to the root object’s generated TypeTable (e.g., FooTypeTable()).
callback must be non-null and valid for the duration of the traversal.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::Register
functions.signature: void flatbuffers::Registry::Register(const char* file_identifier, const char* schema_path)
functions.description: Registers a FlatBuffers schema path under a given file identifier so later conversions can resolve the appropriate schema automatically. Typically called once per schema your application supports, using the 4-character file identifier produced by generated code (e.g., MonsterIdentifier()). Overwrites any existing registration for the same identifier.
requirements: file_identifier should correspond to the schema’s file_identifier (commonly exactly kFileIdentifierLength = 4 characters in FlatBuffers) so lookups succeed (inferred from FlatBuffers conventions and subsequent lookup).
schema_path must be a valid path to a readable schema (.fbs) file on disk; it will be loaded on demand when conversions occur.
Must be called before FlatBufferToText or TextToFlatBuffer for a given identifier.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::FlatBufferToText
functions.signature: bool flatbuffers::Registry::FlatBufferToText(const uint8_t* flatbuf, size_t len, std::string* dest)
functions.description: Converts a FlatBuffer binary to its text representation by extracting the buffer’s file identifier, loading the corresponding registered schema, and generating text. On failure, returns false and sets an internal error message retrievable via GetLastError(). On success, writes the textual output into dest and returns true.
requirements: flatbuf must point to a valid memory region of at least len bytes.
len must be >= sizeof(uoffset_t) + kFileIdentifierLength (otherwise the function returns false with error "buffer truncated").
dest must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::string where the generated text will be stored.
The buffer’s file identifier must have been previously registered via Register; otherwise the function returns false with an error.
The schema file registered for that identifier must be loadable from disk; otherwise the function returns false with an error.
The FlatBuffer content must be valid per the schema; generation errors from GenText will cause the function to return false with an error.
On false return, callers should not use dest’s contents and should call GetLastError() for diagnostics.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::TextToFlatBuffer
functions.signature: flatbuffers::DetachedBuffer flatbuffers::Registry::TextToFlatBuffer(const char* text, const char* file_identifier)
functions.description: Parses FlatBuffers text (JSON-like) into a binary FlatBuffer using the registered schema for the given file identifier. Returns a DetachedBuffer containing the serialized data on success. On failure, returns an empty DetachedBuffer (DetachedBuffer::data() == nullptr) and records a human-readable error accessible via GetLastError().
requirements: text must be a null-terminated C string containing valid FlatBuffers text for the target schema.
file_identifier must correspond to a schema previously registered with Register; otherwise an empty DetachedBuffer is returned.
The schema file registered for that identifier must be loadable and parseable; otherwise an empty DetachedBuffer is returned and an error is set.
Callers must check the returned DetachedBuffer (e.g., data() != nullptr) before using it.
Parsing behavior is affected by options set via SetOptions and include paths set via AddIncludeDirectory (if the schema uses includes).

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::SetOptions
functions.description: Sets parser and generator options that affect subsequent parsing and text generation operations performed by this Registry (e.g., when converting between text and binary).
requirements: opts should be initialized with the desired IDLOptions values before calling.
Must be called before conversion functions to affect those operations; calling afterward does not retroactively change previously performed conversions.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::AddIncludeDirectory
functions.description: Adds a directory to the list of include search paths used by the schema parser when resolving include statements in .fbs files.
requirements: path must point to a valid, existing directory that should be searched for included schema files (required for schemas that use include).

The provided const char* is stored as-is (not copied); the memory backing path must remain valid for as long as the Registry may parse schemas using these include paths (e.g., for the lifetime of the Registry or until paths are no longer needed).
Call before parsing operations that require these include paths (e.g., before FlatBufferToText or TextToFlatBuffer if includes are present).

functions.name: flatbuffers::Registry::GetLastError
functions.description: Returns a reference to the last error message recorded by the Registry during schema loading, parsing, or conversion operations. Use after a function returns failure to obtain diagnostic details.
requirements: Call only after a prior operation fails (e.g., FlatBufferToText returns false or TextToFlatBuffer returns an empty buffer) to retrieve meaningful information.
The returned reference remains valid until the Registry modifies its internal error state (i.e., after subsequent operations) or the Registry is destroyed.

requirements: T should be a pointer type to a compatible FlatBuffers struct (e.g., const MyStruct*).

The returned pointer aliases the underlying buffer; it must not outlive the buffer and must not be used after the buffer is freed or invalidated.

functions.name: flatbuffers::Table::GetVTable
